column1: # paralog_loci.tsv: the loci step 35 (scripts/35-paralogs.sh, Nextflow PARASCOPY) runs Parascopy on.
# One row per Parascopy model; the step runs `parascopy cn-using` once per row, on short reads.
#   model          file name of the model in Parascopy's pinned data (models_GRCh38_1KGP/<population>/),
#   genes          the genes the model's region holds, comma separated
#   region         region of interest, GRCh38 chrom:start-end (1-based, inclusive); a BAM with no read
#                  there gets the row "not assessed" and no Parascopy run
#   reading        what the copy number there means, per value
#   pscn_reliable  yes or no: whether the copy number of each copy (psCN) can be trusted there, or only
#   tag            carrier (a recessive disease gene), SF (ACMG secondary finding), disease (a dominant
#                  or mosaic disease gene not on the SF list), PGx or trait
#   cross_check    another engine that calls the same locus: paraphase (step 35b, HiFi reads), cn-depth
#                  (a row of bin/cn_loci.tsv; RHCE's model covers RHD), or none
#   table          the table's name: <sample>_<table>_copy_number.tsv under paralogs/, and Parascopy's own
#   source         where the reading comes from
# Every row's region lies in its model's main region: SMN1 exon 7 for SMN1, the whole main region for the
# others. agCN counts the copies of all the model's regions together.
# psCN is marked reliable only where it was validated (SMN1); elsewhere the report reads agCN.
# tests/test_paralog_loci.py checks every row against the model list and bin/cn_loci.tsv.

column4: reading
column9: source

column4: psCN of SMN1 at exon 7 (c.840): 0 = the pattern of SMA; 1 = an SMA carrier; 2 or more = not a carrier by copy number (a 2+0 carrier is not ruled out)
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of GBA1 and its pseudogene GBAP1 together, usually 4; under 4 means a copy is missing, as a recombinant GBA1-GBAP1 allele (Gaucher disease) can leave; over 4, an extra copy
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of PMS2 and PMS2CL together, usually 4; under 4 means a deletion in the region, which in PMS2 itself is a cause of Lynch syndrome; which copy lost it is not said
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of STRC and STRCP1 together, usually 4; under 4 means a deletion, and an STRC deletion is a common cause of recessive hearing loss (DFNB16): 3 can be a carrier, 2 can be affected or a pseudogene loss
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of NCF1 and its pseudogenes NCF1B and NCF1C together, usually 6; most recessive chronic granulomatous disease comes from the pseudogenes' GT deletion moved into NCF1, which copy number alone cannot see
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of OTOA and its pseudogene OTOAP1 together, usually 4; under 4 means a deletion, and an OTOA deletion is a cause of recessive hearing loss (DFNB22)
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of the three copies of NEB's triplicate repeat together, usually 6; a gain or loss of a repeat copy is linked to nemaline myopathy
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of the end of CFH and its copy in CFHR1, usually 4; 3 or 2 is the common CFHR3-CFHR1 deletion on one or both chromosomes, which goes with a lower risk of age-related macular degeneration and, on both, with atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Hughes 2006, PMID 16998489; Zipfel 2007, PMID 17367211

column4: agCN of CFHR4 and its copy in CFHR3, usually 4; under 4 means a deletion in the CFHR cluster, such as the CFHR3-CFHR1 deletion
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Zipfel 2007, PMID 17367211

column4: agCN of C4A and C4B together, the number of C4 genes, usually 4 and often 2 to 6; more C4A copies go with a higher risk of schizophrenia
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Sekar 2016, PMID 26814963

column4: agCN of RHCE and the RHD sequence it shares, usually 4: a cross-check of the RHD row of bin/cn_loci.tsv (the RHD deletion of RhD-negative people), 3 with one RHD copy, 2 with none
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of GYPA with GYPB and GYPE (the MNS blood group genes), usually 6; under 6 means a deletion of one of them
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of FCGR3A and FCGR3B together, usually 4; FCGR3B copy number varies, and low FCGR3B copy number goes with lupus nephritis
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Aitman 2006, PMID 16482158

column4: agCN of FCGR2A and FCGR2C together, usually 4; a change is a copy-number variant of the FCGR locus
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of FCGR1A and its copies on chr1, usually 2 for each copy the reference holds
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of CD177 and its pseudogene copies, usually 4; CD177 carries the neutrophil antigen HNA-2
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of the tryptase genes TPSB2 and TPSAB1 together, usually 4; extra copies are hereditary alpha-tryptasemia only when they are alpha-tryptase copies of TPSAB1, which copy number alone cannot tell
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Lyons 2016, PMID 27749843

column4: agCN of HSPA1A and HSPA1B together, usually 4
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of KLRC2 (NKG2C) and its copies, usually 4; under 4 can be the common KLRC2 deletion on one or both chromosomes
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Miyashita 2004, PMID 14688071

column4: agCN of the alpha-defensin genes DEFA1, DEFA1B and DEFA3 together, which varies widely between people
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of CHRNA7 and its partial copy CHRFAM7A together, usually 4; CHRFAM7A copy number varies between people
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of HYDIN and its copy HYDIN2 together, usually 4; HYDIN is a gene of recessive primary ciliary dyskinesia
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of the salivary amylase genes AMY1A, AMY1B and AMY1C together, usually 6 and between 2 and 15 in Perry 2007; more copies go with more salivary amylase
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Perry 2007, PMID 17828263

column4: agCN of APOBEC3A and the APOBEC3B part it shares, usually 4; 3 or 2 is the common 29.5 kb APOBEC3B deletion on one or both chromosomes
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Kidd 2007, PMID 17447845

column4: agCN of ABCC6 and its pseudogene copies, usually 6; under 6 means a deletion, and ABCC6 is the gene of recessive pseudoxanthoma elasticum
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of VWF exons 23-34 and their pseudogene VWFP1 together, usually 4; VWF is the gene of von Willebrand disease
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of PROS1 and its pseudogene PROS2P together, usually 4; PROS1 is the gene of protein S deficiency
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of SORD and its pseudogene SORD2P together, usually 4; SORD neuropathy comes mostly from a one-base deletion the pseudogene carries, which copy number alone cannot see
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Cortese 2020, PMID 32367058

column4: agCN of GTF2I and its copies at the edges of the Williams-Beuren region, usually 2 for each copy the reference holds; under that means a deletion
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of GTF2H2C and GTF2H2 in the SMA region, usually 4; GTF2H2 can be lost with SMN1 in spinal muscular atrophy
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869

column4: agCN of NOTCH2 and its NOTCH2NL copies together, which varies between people; NOTCH2 is a gene of Alagille syndrome
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of KRT6C with KRT6A and KRT6B, usually 2 for each copy the reference holds; the KRT6 genes are genes of pachyonychia congenita
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of KRT86 and its copy, usually 2 for each copy the reference holds; KRT86 is a gene of monilethrix
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of PLG and its copies on chr2, usually 2 for each copy the reference holds; PLG is the gene of recessive plasminogen deficiency
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of PIK3CA and its pseudogene copy on chr22, usually 4; germline copy number only: the mosaic PIK3CA variants of overgrowth are not assessed
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Mandelker 2016, PMID 27228465

column4: agCN of CEL and its pseudogene CELP together, usually 4; a CEL-CELP hybrid allele goes with chronic pancreatitis
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869; Fjeld 2015, PMID 25774637

column4: agCN of MUC5B and its copies, usually 2 for each copy the reference holds
column9: Prodanov and Bansal 2022, PMID 35680869
